RU-4.plain: Vanilla's dated abandoned-settlement marker with no loot; useful only as an anchor for another route.

RU-5.plain: Rebuild by founding a new outpost on the same tile at full price; nothing of the old one is remembered.

SM-1.plain: Vanilla bases with re-authored defenders for tier flavour. Easy, but not hard enough on its own.

SM-2.plain: Varied generated walled bases per faction, with more defenders; tier set by which layouts a faction uses. Data only.

SM-3.plain: Hand-built castles and forts with walls, siege engines and placed defenders; the same fort every time.

SM-4.plain: Garrison size follows a curve we choose, e.g. tech tier, and can remember losses from an earlier assault.

SM-5.plain: One named settlement always generates as a set-piece citadel while its siblings stay generated; for places the plot names.

SM-6.plain: Vanilla's own structure generator builds a different surface fortress each time; tribal or medieval looks need authored rooms.

SM-7.plain: Defenders call reinforcements mid-assault; killing the caller stops them, and the base falls on a condition we set.

TERRITORY-06.R1.plain: The taken settlement becomes a player-held world marker that remembers its old faction. No people, no map to run.

TERRITORY-06.R2.plain: The settlement stays in its faction but is marked as the colony's; its map, defenders and trader remain the faction's.

TERRITORY-06.R4.plain: A record at faction level, for whole factions that swear themselves to the colony and for the Schism's successor.

TERRITORY-06.R5.plain: Vanilla's ally behaviour, such as gifts, traders and help when raided, covers part of the payout. Partial only.

TERRITORY-06.R0+R3.plain: Vanilla Factions Expanded Empire's tithes: the Church's perk for a titled colonist, not a conquered holding. Widening it is not recommended.

TERRITORY-06.R6+R7.plain: RimPacts or Faction Territories as shipped. Not recommended: neither works in multiplayer.

TERRITORY-07.P1.plain: Reuse Vanilla Factions Expanded Empire's tithe engine for payload, cadence and accrual, with a readable due date.

TERRITORY-07.P2.plain: Vanilla Expanded's five delivery methods, such as a pack animal walking in or a stockpile left on the tile.

TERRITORY-07.P3.plain: The player calls for a drop of goods or pawns where they point, on a cooldown.

TERRITORY-07.P4.plain: The rebuild debt shows on the holding's tile and is paid by a caravan standing there; nothing flows until it's paid.

TERRITORY-07.P6.plain: Gifts and ally traffic arriving unprompted on the storyteller's own clock.

TERRITORY-07.P5.plain: Accrued credit spent on the holding's menu. Ruled out: the requirement allows no holding currency.

SF-1.plain: Vanilla already hints: trader-caravan letters name the trader type, and a slaver tribe is readable from its beliefs.

SF-2.plain: Each faction's specialty declared in its definition, public from the start.

SF-3.plain: A faction's specialty hidden until first contact: an envoy, caravan, comms call or meeting.

SS-1.plain: Each settlement draws one of several trade profiles for its faction. Can't read the tile, and changes if the settlement is conquered.

SS-2.plain: Specialty computed from the tile's biome, terrain and features plus the faction. Nothing stored, so later balance edits shift it.

SS-3.plain: Specialty rolled once and saved per tile; can be hand-placed and survives conquest, era change and balance edits.

SS-5.plain: No settlement layer, only the faction's specialty. The requirement still holds.

SS-4.plain: Different settlement types at world generation. Not recommended: a weaker version of storing it per tile.

SV-1.plain: Revealed when a caravan arrives to visit, trade, gift or attack.

SV-3.plain: Revealed when a caravan passes within range, or at a roadside meeting.

SV-4.plain: A scouting outpost reveals the settlements within its range.

SV-5.plain: First contact reveals the faction's specialty only.

SV-2.plain: Revealed by opening trade there; the stock itself shows the specialty.

SV-6.plain: Everything public from the start. Fails the requirement.

SD-0.plain: Remove or disable 'Show sellable items' until the settlement is learned. Required whatever else is chosen.

SD-1..SD-11.plain: Where learned facts show: inspect line, settlement tab, attack menu, info card, map badge, map overlay, world search, own tab, Factions tab, reveal letter, Alt-hover.

SW-1.plain: Faction names, descriptions, icons and art stop implying a tech tier. Data only, but vanilla's legibility is lost for everyone.

SW-2+SW-4.plain: Neutral map icons for unlearned settlements, or removing World Tech Level's 'Tech level' line from faction tooltips.

SW-3.plain: A faction's label, icon and description stay neutral on the Factions tab and elsewhere until the faction is known.

SW-5.plain: Withhold tier text in RimPacts' war and puppet windows. Not recommended: those only address factions already engaged.

SP-1.plain: Hide 'Trading here requires title' on an unlearned settlement; the rule itself stays.

SP-2.plain: Same result as SP-1 by a more fragile method. Not recommended.

SP-3.plain: Delete the Empire's trade-permit rule, so the line vanishes because anyone may trade. Changes a rule instead of withholding it.

TR-1.plain: The holding's era is stored at conquest, from its former faction; only payment changes it.

TR-2.plain: Era read live from the former faction. Not recommended: holdings climb for free whenever the parent does.

TR-3.plain: Era held in the holding's definition, one per era; advancing swaps it, which is messy for world objects.

TR-4.plain: Advance by handing the settlement to an existing later-era faction, so its map and defenders visibly modernize. Only for holdings kept in their faction.

TG-1.plain: Gate: a holding can't advance past the colony's current era.

TG-2.plain: Gate: only after the former parent faction has itself climbed an era.

TG-3.plain: Gate: a research project must be finished first.

TG-4.plain: No gate beyond the price and a cooldown.

H-L1..H-L4.plain: Release: return it to its parent, cede it, abandon it, or let the parent buy it back. Only ceding to a randomly drawn faction conforms.

H-T2.plain: The parent demands 'return it or we come'; refusing brings an attack. The holding goes only by the player's choice.

H-T1.plain: A timed attack at the holding: go and fight, or lose it. Hard alone, medium if the ally-battle machinery exists.

H-T4.plain: Break the enemy's staging camp near the holding before its deadline, or lose the holding.

H-T3.plain: A warning, then one to four counter-attack waves over several weeks. Hard.

H-T6.plain: The parent stops honouring the arrangement, with a grace-period quest to make it a moment. Only for holdings kept in their faction.

H-T5.plain: RimPacts' silent reversion to the original owner. Not recommended: its code never actually runs.

H-D1.plain: A named faction burns the holding. Doesn't conform as written, since a lost holding must pass to a random faction.

H-D2.plain: The colony razes its own holding.

H-O1.plain: Unrest builds through grievance events the player answers one by one; past a threshold, a retake demand or attack follows.

H-O2.plain: RimPacts' quarterly revolt roll. Not recommended: silent, random, and no multiplayer.

H-V.plain: Vanilla Factions Expanded Empire's 'release all vassals', only for its own tithe vassals.

MO-F1.plain: Instantly move everyone into a caravan on the tile, close the map, then transfer. The only option that fits the era advance.

MO-W1.plain: Queue the change until the players leave the map; suits the Schism, revolts and conquest, but may wait indefinitely.

MO-W2+W3+F2+F3.plain: Variants: a visible countdown then forced exit, hold the whole advance while such a map is open, a forced pack-up window, or eject straight home.

MO-A.plain: Transfer anyway. Not recommended: the settlement counts as defeated, or the party is lost or kidnapped.

MO-S.plain: Skip that settlement. Not recommended: it keeps its old owner for good, leaving the world half-changed.

GV-1.plain: Forbid landing the gravship on NPC settlements so the case never arises; costs Odyssey's land-on-an-enemy-base assault.

GV-3+GV-5.plain: Transfer with the ship still there, and stop its takeoff erasing the settlement. Breaks the never-while-loaded rule for this case.

GV-7.plain: Hold the era advance until the ship leaves. Breaks no rule, but waits on the players.

GV-2.plain: Skip that settlement at the advance; it keeps its old owner for good. Breaks the era rules.

GV-4.plain: Change it once the ship leaves: a forbidden delay that may never end.

GV-6.plain: Force the ship to take off. Not recommended: it can't finish in one step and isn't multiplayer-safe.

CF-B.plain: Caravans, pods and aircraft bound there stop, with a letter naming the new owner; closes the attacking-an-ally hazard.

CF-C.plain: Re-aim the caravan: at the recreated settlement, to what the new relation allows, or on to the old owner's nearest settlement.

CF-E.plain: Vanilla behaviour stands, but the transfer letter names the affected caravans.

CF-G.plain: Attack orders refuse once the target's owner changes, whoever made the transfer, other mods included.

CF-F.plain: The arrival becomes a scene with the new owner at the gate: parley, a toll, or being turned away.

CF-A.plain: Vanilla as is. Not recommended alone: orders stall unexplained, and attack orders can land on allies.

CF-D.plain: Don't transfer settlements with anything inbound. Not for the era advance: they'd keep their old owner for good.

OS-1.plain: Vanilla comms requests: a trade caravan, orbital trader or military aid, priced in Goodwill. Needs a console and Ally; troops only from Industrial factions.

OS-2.plain: Title-free permits granted by Reverence band, used from the royal aid menu on cooldowns: troops, lent labourers, goods drops, a shuttle.

OS-3.plain: Our own comms options, shown locked with their Reverence threshold and priced in Goodwill; can start a quest or send troops.

OS-4.plain: A shop-like menu of the faction's services, each a quest, priced in Goodwill behind a minimum-Goodwill gate.

OS-5.plain: Always-on perks by band: reinforcements when raided, better trade prices, periodic donations, recruiting its visitors. Received, never asked.

OS-6.plain: Offers, visits, gifts and help arrive unasked, at a frequency the Reverence band sets.

OS-7.plain: A fixed basket or labour on a clock, e.g. one labourer each quarter. The route nearest to paying goods.

OS-8.plain: People lent for a term who then leave, or offered as a reward the player picks; never dumped on the colony.

OS-9.plain: A caravan at a sworn settlement asks in person for guides, recruits, resupply or shelter.

OS-10.plain: A signal fire the colony builds summons the faction's warband; works in the Neolithic, before any comms console.

TERRITORY-13.U1.plain: RimPacts' treaties and tributaries. Not recommended: no multiplayer sync, and it creates factions.

PRESSURE-01.A.plain: Our own storytellers keep Cassandra, Randy and Phoebe's temperaments but recompute threat points from these inputs, between a floor and ceiling.

PRESSURE-02.A.plain: Our own storytellers plus a pacing component whose firing rate follows enemy count and era time. Re-authors three vanilla curves.

PRESSURE-03.A.plain: Cap the cost of each faction's most expensive pawn, pushing raids toward elite units. Data only; must be tuned with raid tactics' minimum sizes.

PRESSURE-03.B.plain: An era's signature raid becomes possible only above a strength band. Data only.

PRESSURE-04.Size.plain: Enemy count adds to raid size, through the strength formula.

PRESSURE-04.Frequency.plain: Enemy count raises how often hostile events fire, through the pacing component.

PRESSURE-04.a.plain: Vanilla Expanded's allies-reduce-threats option. Data only, but coarse, inverted from what's wanted, and blind to Reverence.

PRESSURE-04.b.plain: Our own weighting by enemy count, Reverence band and era; expresses 'enemies increase threats' directly.

PRESSURE-05.A.plain: Vanilla Expanded's special raid type fixes faction, points and tactic in data. Omitting the points range silently gives a zero-strength raid.

PRESSURE-06.A.plain: A second pacing component driven by global Reverence fires our pilgrim, offering and volunteer events on vanilla visitor, trader and wanderer mechanics.

PRESSURE-07.U1.plain: Fire beats from the campaign's spine quest, never from a random storyteller component, so chance never decides them.

PRESSURE-07.U2.plain: A temporary game condition that quiets competing threats around a beat.

PRESSURE-07.U3.plain: Put a beat's event in a special category that random components can't pick.

PRESSURE-07.U4.plain: Set a minimum or fixed strength for a beat's raid, so it never arrives under-strength.

PRESSURE-08.A.plain: One raid behaviour driven by per-aim settings, one raid type per aim with a titled letter, plus our own trigger for partial success.

PRESSURE-09.A.plain: Raid size scales with how much that particular faction hates the colony.

PRESSURE-09.B.plain: A named enemy raids on its own schedule, apart from the general storyteller.

PRESSURE-09.C.plain: A declared war as a quest: its own raid rhythm, visible in the Quests tab, ended by a signal such as peace.

PRESSURE-09.D.plain: The world generates hostility, e.g. taking settlements caps goodwill, with vanilla's letter and faction-card reason. Immediate, no new state.

PRESSURE-09.E.plain: A named per-faction grudge that runs past −100 and can escalate, decay or be spent.

PRESSURE-09.F.plain: Hated factions use non-raid actions too: sieges, caravan demands, ambushes, refusing trade. Data only.

PRESSURE-09.G.plain: Hated factions are picked more often when the storyteller chooses who raids.

PRESSURE-10.A.plain: A small readout feeding the campaign's political screen; which screen shows it is still undecided.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T1.plain: One offer on a fixed day. If nothing qualifies that day, it's lost for good with no warning.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T2.plain: Offered after a set day, and re-offered some days after it lapses unaccepted. Has a multiplayer joining edge case.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T3.plain: Joins the random quest pool after a set day; may never come, or may recur.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T4.plain: Our own timer: after day X it keeps retrying until the offer can actually be made. Fixes the fixed-day miss.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T7.plain: A Vanilla Expanded quest chain offers it on a day drawn from a range, whatever the storyteller; generates even when broken.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T5.plain: Our own game-level timer. Not recommended: the storyteller-based retrying timer does the same job.

ENCOUNTERS-01.T6.plain: Put it in Charting's pool. Not recommended: wrong channel, and it can't be selected there.

ENCOUNTERS-02.G1.plain: Any non-hostile faction at random. Can't filter by a goodwill number or by culture.

ENCOUNTERS-02.G2.plain: A named faction leader asks, with chosen faction types excluded; the letter names the person.

ENCOUNTERS-02.G3.plain: Our own filter for a minimum goodwill number, or tribal factions only.

ENCOUNTERS-03.S1.plain: A generated site under the giver's faction with its people and an anima tree. One visit only; it vanishes once left.

ENCOUNTERS-03.S2.plain: A map-less meeting on arrival, shaped like peace talks. Cheaper for the player, less vivid, and needs our code.

ENCOUNTERS-04.V2.plain: Visitors walk to the tree, venerate it and leave, like Ideology's reliquary pilgrims; colonists only watch. Needs Ideology.

ENCOUNTERS-04.V1.plain: Visitors loiter at the colony's edge and leave; the tree features only in the letter. Data only.

ENCOUNTERS-04.V3.plain: Our own rite in which a colonist takes part alongside the visitors. Hard.

ENCOUNTERS-05.U1.plain: A re-readable passage, a fading memory, an inert mark on a pawn, or an event that beliefs react to. Data only.

ENCOUNTERS-05.U2.plain: A techprint unlocking research; only for projects the player can also reach another way.

ENCOUNTERS-05.U3.plain: A remembered fact that later quests can check: did the colony learn it?

ENCOUNTERS-05.U4.plain: A readable lore object, at the site or carried home.

ENCOUNTERS-06.A.plain: The offer expires with no failure consequence, an unvisited site times out, and the anima linking ritual is ruled out.

TRACE-01.A.plain: Our own copy of VFE Deserters' Visibility ladder without needing that mod: a proven band-and-effects design, but a sizeable build.

TRACE-02.A.plain: Each hack adds Trace by the target's depth, quests carry plus or minus Trace, analysis adds as it runs, and Trace fades daily.

TRACE-03.A.plain: Two band effects: one blocks or allows specific incidents, one raises the Glitterites' odds of being the raider. Raid size scales only inside the pursuit.

TRACE-04.A.plain: A permanent, auto-accepted pursuit quest holds the search; the countdown stays hidden until the reveal, then is recalculated from current Trace whenever shown.

TRACE-05.A.plain: Vanilla's raid quest pieces in the same shape as Royalty's endgame 'survive the raids' quest; cheap, pure data.

TRACE-06.A.plain: Each world tick, check whether the colony's tile changed and how far. Simple and safe; the escape registers a tick after landing, not instantly.

TRACE-07.A.plain: Free: the existing distance check already treats a cross-layer move as infinitely far. Holds today by accident; one later change could silently break it.

TRACE-07.B.plain: An explicit layer-change check: gives a named 'we left the planet' story event and a sturdier rule. Variant: count only entering or leaving space.

TRACE-07.C.plain: A separate escape distance authored per layer, so orbit-to-orbit moves get a sensible threshold; the only route that answers moves within orbit.

TRACE-07.D.plain: Detect the move the instant the gravship lands. Faster, but runs outside Multiplayer's safe window and fights other mods over the hook. Not recommended.

TRACE-08.A.plain: Each colony gets its own hidden search, reveal, raids and escape on its own clock; one can be found while the other is safe.

TRACE-08.Aprime.plain: Per colony, with each search meter on the colony's own map: removes one Multiplayer clock hazard, but a short move must carry progress by hand.

TRACE-08.B.plain: Only one named colony, such as the gravship, is ever hunted; the other is a permanent haven. Smallest build, no Multiplayer work.

TRACE-08.C.plain: One countdown for the whole faction; detection and repeat raids hit every colony, so splitting up doesn't help. The search runs on one colony's clock.

TRACE-09.A.plain: Six readouts: band in the network window, Trace on quest offers, optional per-hack cost, band-change letter, quest-tab countdown, number always on screen.

CURRENCIES-01.A.plain: One saved store for both, a network tab and a line under the date. As pure numbers they miss the top-left resource list. Large build.

CURRENCIES-02.a.plain: Take VFE Deserters' Intel whole: Intel becomes rotting, lootable cargo, and buying needs a war with the Church first. Least code, fragile in Multiplayer.

CURRENCIES-02.b.plain: Our own stored balance and exchange, as the spec builds: no rot or loss, spendable anywhere, earnable from lore. Most code.

CURRENCIES-02.c.plain: Our own Intel item and vendor: free stockpile readout without Deserters' baggage, but lore can never pay Intel, and Multiplayer is untested.

CURRENCIES-03.A.plain: A currency line among a quest's reward choices, plus a grant step for hand-written quests.

CURRENCIES-04.Analysis.plain: Artifact dismantling pays Intel in instalments as it progresses; a one-shot use item was rejected because an interruption loses everything.

CURRENCIES-04.Lore.plain: Studying a lore object at a site credits Intel directly, or a site quest grants it when the player investigates.

CURRENCIES-05.A.plain: A decoder building at home, always usable once built, paced by its own research. Plot-critical items should be sold here.

CURRENCIES-05.B.plain: A faction broker such as the Traders Guild; needs goodwill, comms and the faction revealed, so it can close on the player.

CURRENCIES-06.A.plain: Vanilla Expanded Framework's quest shop with our currencies plugged in; less work, needs Multiplayer sync work.

CURRENCIES-06.B.plain: Our own quest catalogue from scratch, the fallback if VEF is declined; several times the code.

CURRENCIES-07.A.plain: One shelf for everything; an item is sold as a small quest that rewards the item. Pure data.

CURRENCIES-07.B.plain: Each entry leaves and restocks the shelf on its own timer.

CURRENCIES-07.C.plain: Our own eligibility check, so an entry can require an era, a balance or a political flag, not only research.

CURRENCIES-07.D.plain: Two shelves: VEF's shop for missions, our Intel exchange for items.

CURRENCIES-07.E.plain: Reskin a vanilla trader as the shop; costly and cannot sell a mission. Not recommended.

CURRENCIES-08.A.plain: Put a freshly generated version of the same mission back on the shelf.

CURRENCIES-08.B.plain: Refund the price when the mission fails; usable as a per-entry option.

CURRENCIES-08.C.plain: Re-offer it free as an ordinary quest outside the shop; cheap, but also hands it out free at game start. Not for plot missions.

CURRENCIES-08.D.plain: For Schism steps, the chain simply re-offers the failed step.

CURRENCIES-08.E.plain: Use VFE Deserters' shop; its service missions never come back. Not recommended.

CURRENCIES-09.A.plain: Schism steps wait in order in a catalogue, with favours alongside; buying one charges and starts it in one action.

CURRENCIES-09.B.plain: Steps arrive as ordinary quest offers marked 'requires N Influence', charged on acceptance; offers must not expire, and Multiplayer needs care.

CURRENCIES-09.C.plain: One VEF quest giver for plot and favours; loses the step order and discards favours on reset. Not recommended.

CURRENCIES-09.D.plain: Adopt VFE Deserters as the Schism wholesale; arrives in the wrong era and offers a sell-out. Not recommended as shipped.

CURRENCIES-10.U1.plain: Either physical Intel items rot, or the stored balance loses a set amount daily, as Trace does. Effort not yet assessed.

HACKING-01.A.plain: Ushanka's Hacking Expansion security tiers plus two Ultra tiers, and a fix so a target always gets its highest qualifying tier.

HACKING-02.A.plain: Tag each target with a class; the hack is refused with a readable reason until the matching project is done.

HACKING-03.A.plain: Standard research gating on studied Glitterite objects, optionally plus an Intel-bought item; pure data, cheap.

HACKING-04.A.plain: Reuse Ushanka's eight abilities, learned from hacked data items and re-gated behind Glitterite items and Ultra research; each wholly new ability is extra code.

HACKING-05.A.plain: Works as shipped with Ushanka and Odyssey's security terminal; a small fix stops a seized turret staying mis-targeted.

HACKING-06.A.plain: A relay item on the field colonist swaps in the home hacker's hacking stats; the field colonist still does the work.

HACKING-06.B.plain: Mechanitor-style control across maps; far larger, and adds a capacity cap nobody asked for. Not selected.

HACKING-07.A.plain: An intrusion log entry raised whenever a hack completes or the hacker is locked out.

HACKING-08.A.plain: Mostly existing interface; intrusion history becomes a Cyberpod tab, with a letter per deep intrusion as the cheap fallback.

ANDROIDS-01.A.plain: VRE – Android's production line as shipped; an android is a human xenotype, so faith and devotion work unchanged. Needs Multiplayer Compatibility's entry.

ANDROIDS-02.A.plain: A normal research gate on a studied exemplar, pure data; holds only if the research shortcuts are also shut off.

ANDROIDS-03.A.plain: Every android can hold and use a psylink: simple, but a fact about the whole species, and it strips their shield against psychic attacks.

ANDROIDS-03.B.plain: Chosen per android at the creation station; a hearing android loses synthetic immunity and can catch disease, addiction and cancer.

ANDROIDS-03.C.plain: Awakened androids may also link at an anima tree; stacks on top of A or B.

ANDROIDS-03.D.plain: Gate it on a story condition such as a flag, the altar or the era; also reopens neuroformer upgrades. Needs code, fragile on VRE updates.

ANDROIDS-03.E.plain: Leave androids psychically deaf, as a stated cost of an artificial body.

ANDROIDS-04.K1.plain: Control who may be granted a psylink: the rite already admits only awakened androids and refuses prisoners.

ANDROIDS-04.K2.plain: Awakening lifts deafness: basic androids stay deaf, awakened ones hear, with no disease cost.

ANDROIDS-04.K3.plain: Per-android choice at the station, with arrived androids set by xenotype; carries the disease cost and a station loophole for prisoners.

ANDROIDS-04.K4.plain: Each kind carries its own marker gene deciding deaf or hearing; the only data route separating built from arrived androids.

ANDROIDS-04.K5.plain: Our own sensitivity rule; the only way to make deafness absolute, even against psychic gear or lost eyes.

ANDROIDS-05.A.plain: Vanilla's no-faith and unrecruitable flags; cheap but leaky: a faithless prisoner converts at the first try, and difficulty settings undo it.

ANDROIDS-05.B.plain: Hide every recruit, enslave and convert option, so the player sees a clear 'no'; other mods acting directly can still slip through.

ANDROIDS-05.C.plain: Block the outcome where every path converges; absolute, but refusals can leave broken states, like a freed hostile prisoner. Meant as B's backstop.

ANDROIDS-06.J1.plain: A surgery consuming a persona subcore that, in one step, removes the Glitterite mark, awakens it, gives it a faith and recruits it.

ANDROIDS-06.J2.plain: Done in VRE's android modification station, patched: pick its subroutines gene by gene, but it consumes nothing without extra work.

ANDROIDS-06.J3.plain: The operation only unlocks it; the colony then recruits it the normal way, with no restored personality. Cheapest.

ANDROIDS-06.J4.plain: A ritual of the player's faith; drags in ritual quality and precepts. Not recommended.

ANDROIDS-06.J5.plain: A dedicated jailbreak machine; a big build that J1 already covers. Not recommended.

ANDROIDS-07.A.plain: Delete the 2% awakened-android chance from those factions; a tiny data patch, but it also removes them at Ultra.

ANDROIDS-07.B.plain: Hand-authored faction spawn pools: a faction fields an android only if we write one in.

HF-1+HF-2.plain: Write every faction and every reachable pawn type ourselves, so none inherits the android chance; a large volume of data.

ANDROIDS.HF-4.plain: A check at pawn creation that rejects any xenotype not on the faction's list; the only route that also catches code-spawned pawns.

RESEARCH-01.A.plain: Vanilla's study-to-unlock requirement with the object kept; works at any tech level, pure data. Needs Biotech.

RESEARCH-02.A.plain: Vanilla techprints, quest rewards that unlock a fixed project, and the Intel exchange; pure data.

RESEARCH-03.A.plain: Craft trial pieces from the resource and have a researcher take each apart; paid up front, a failure letter per trial. Needs Biotech.

RESEARCH-03.B.plain: Craft the project's own techprints from the resource, then research normally; the prints leak to traders and loot unless excluded.

RESEARCH-03.C.plain: Ushanka's item that turns into research points when used; speeds research, but is not a cost.

RESEARCH-03.D.plain: More Realistic Research's experimental-materials system; that mod is declined. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-03.E.plain: A special bench burns the resource while research runs and stops when empty; the only route that consumes during research.

RESEARCH-03.F.plain: Our own per-project cost list, paid at start; A and B already do this. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-04.A.plain: Vanilla's study-over-time loop with our payouts added; progress is saved on the item across interruptions.

RESEARCH-04.B.plain: Our version of the bench 'Analyze' order; an interrupted session is lost, and it tangles with exemplar gates. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-04.C.plain: A long crafting bill at a workstation; cannot target one specific artifact, and cancelling can lose it.

RESEARCH-04.D.plain: A single timed use of the item; any interruption loses all progress. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-04.E.plain: VEF's studiable building; works only on buildings, with no saved progress. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-04.F.plain: Fully custom; it just rebuilds route A. Not recommended.

RESEARCH-05.A.plain: One patch file switching off each offending source, a one-line fix to vanilla's Schematic book, and a script that audits every mod.

RESEARCH-06.A.plain: Gate a whole build-menu category on research in pure data; it shows greyed and refuses with a message rather than hiding.

RESEARCH-06.B.plain: Our own system, modelled on VFE Tribals, locking individual work types and orders like mining or hunting until researched.

ERA-01.A.plain: The era advances the moment the capstone research completes. Simplest trigger, with no ceremony attached.

ERA-01.B.plain: A celebrated rite fires the advance on success; a failed or cancelled rite advances nothing. The advance becomes a performed beat that can fail.

ERA-01.C.plain: The capstone itself demands a build, resources or exemplars first, so the advance waits on a physical achievement, not just research.

ERA-02.A.plain: Remove World Tech Level's change-era button, which also removes its add-factions window, and keep its faction filter off. The only route.

ERA-03.U1.plain: The era log itself: an append-only record of every boundary crossed. Needed whichever clock is chosen.

ERA-03.A.plain: One world clock for everyone, ticking whenever either colony plays. Simple, but era time rises while the other player is playing.

ERA-03.B.plain: Each colony keeps its own era clock, running only while it plays. Fair per colony, but day-keyed beats fire at different moments for each.

ERA-04.A.plain: World Tech Level already shows the era on the planet tab for free; we add an 'era began: day N' line and a boundary-log row.

AE-1.plain: A scenario setting switches the content off for the game. Home-only for dangers and the walker, but strips road wrecks from every map.

AE-2.plain: Delete the content from the map generator lists by patch, as Medieval Overhaul does. Same reach as the scenario setting: wrecks vanish everywhere.

AE-3.plain: A blocking step added only to player-colony maps, so wrecks and ruins vanish at home while maps you travel to keep them.

AE-4.plain: World Tech Level's filter holds content back until its era, but only on maps made later, and it also strips encounter maps. Not recommended.

AE-5a.plain: Reaching Industrial itself delivers the mechanitor crash quest. Reliable one-time timing; needs code.

AE-5b.plain: A storyteller event unlocked at Industrial delivers the crash. Easy, but it could fire more than once without a guard.

AE-6.plain: The crashed walker stays in the yard, but its transponder can't be decrypted until Industrial. The Ultra-tech wreck is visible from day one.

AE-9.plain: At an era advance, a sealed vault 'that was always there' appears on the living home map. Untested and hard; wrong for debris.

AE-7.plain: Era-fitting debris or an authored structure sits where the ruin would have been. Props are easy; hostile defenders need code. Open from day one.

AE-8.plain: The content becomes a place to travel to: an Archon site on a nearby tile, offered by quest or the transponder. Going is a choice.

AB-1.plain: Configure Ignorance Is Bliss. Cheap, but it only weights and vetoes when the game picks the faction; quests, caravan meetings and orbital traders slip through.

AB-2.plain: World Tech Level's per-event, per-quest era ceiling. A hard cap on what can fire, but it never picks factions, and every def needs a row.

AB-3.plain: Our own gate on every faction arrival, with an explicit exemption for authored breaches. The full hard rule; the quest half is near-hard to build.

DP-1.plain: Before Industrial, delivered goods and people simply appear at the map edge or trade spot, no pod. One patch covers everything.

DP-2.plain: A courier or pack animal walks the goods in, drops them and leaves. Nicer flavour; hard if the courier must survive the trip.

DP-3.plain: Pawn rewards and wandering joiners walk in from the edge instead of dropping in. Narrow and cheap.

DP-4.plain: Called military aid arrives on foot instead of by pod, while Industrial allies still drop. A small data change.

HF-1.plain: Write every faction definition ourselves, including those vanilla and mods spawn mid-game. Controls which pawn types a faction lists, not what they carry.

HF-2.plain: Write every pawn type factions can use, with private gear tags and explicit xenotypes, so mod items join only by our choice. Large volume.

HF-3.plain: Rewrite the pawn types the game and quests summon outside any faction: refugees, slaves, drifters and the like. Closes the side doors.

ERA.HF-4.plain: One check on every pawn as it is generated, stripping or swapping anything off-list. The only route that catches mod code and recycled pawns.

HF-5.plain: World Tech Level caps pawn tech at the era. An easy backstop, but not authored, and it downgrades the Glitterites' xenotypes too.

CHARTING-01.A.plain: Build on vanilla's long-range scanner job with a second progress track. Vanilla supplies operator work, random finds, the guaranteed-find timer and saved progress.

CHARTING-02.A.plain: A parent quest issues each story beat as a sub-quest, like vanilla's Archonexus chain, driven by apparatus work rather than a timer.

CHARTING-02.B.plain: VEF's quest-chain gates. Easy, but fires on its own clock, so it suits side content only, not the main spine.

CHARTING-03.A.plain: Tag quests as pool members and let vanilla's own quest weighting pace them. Adding a quest is a one-line patch.

CHARTING-04.A.plain: Each quest carries an 'announced from' era; our code switches it from charted to storyteller-offered at each advance. Recommended; no game patching.

CHARTING-04.B.plain: Two copies of each quest: a charted one, and a storyteller one World Tech Level hides until its era. Easy; leans on that mod.

CHARTING-04.C.plain: An era check inside the quest itself. Not recommended: traders and books hand out quests without running the check.

CHARTING-04.D.plain: Patch the storyteller's quest chooser. Not recommended: adds nothing over the 'announced from' era.

CHARTING-05.A.plain: Hard minimum and maximum distance bands, a registry of mobility rungs, capped by the apparatus tier. A new rung is one data block.

CHARTING-05.U1.plain: Optional extra: bias finds toward the near end of a band. Custom code; cost not stated.

CHARTING-06.A.plain: One shared mechanism; each tier is just a building, a work job and a research project. Cheap to extend.

CHARTING-07.A.plain: Two progress bars without vanilla's estimate, a Waystone status line, a reason in each arrival letter, and the chain count in the quest tab.

CHARTING-08.A.plain: Every tile a caravan enters rolls for a find, on foot or in vehicles; flying never counts. One patch on an unused seam.

CHARTING-08.B.plain: The same rolls without patching the game, via a component on each caravan type. More bookkeeping per caravan.

CHARTING-08.C.plain: Copy Faction Territories' version. Not recommended: it misses vehicle caravans and its timer isn't saved.

CHARTING-08.D.plain: Outposts search on their own: which types look, how often, how far, pausing while a find is unresolved. Built on VEF Outposts.

CHARTING-08.E.plain: The find arrives as a quest rather than a bare map marker, still placed next to whoever found it.

CHARTING-09.A.plain: A readable object on site, studied by right-click order. Pays Intel once, signals the quest, archives a letter, becomes a 'read' object.

CHARTING-09.B.plain: A record looted as a book, hauled home and read there. Flagged as possible only; not designed.

CHARTING-10.A.plain: Charting works orbit too; the scanner is removed or reskinned as an apparatus tier. Discovery stays labour, and the reveal gate is one check.

CHARTING-10.B.plain: The passive orbital scanner delivers Charting's orbital content. Easy for everyday sites, but not labour, and story beats need code.

CHARTING-10.C.plain: Two instruments sharing pools: Charting keeps the story; the scanner is a passive orbital survey eye. Needs a requirement amended.

CHARTING-10.D.plain: Keep them fully separate, vanilla as shipped. Nothing to build, but orbit plays like somebody else's game.

INFRA-01.A.plain: Remove ancient roads and stone roads from world generation, leaving paths and tracks. Must be decided before the world is made.

INFRA-01.U1.plain: A five-step speed ladder across road tiers. Pure data, retunable any time.

INFRA-01.U2.plain: Mark isolated factions, such as the anima tribe, to never join the road network. One field per faction.

INFRA-02.A.plain: One setting per road tier that applies to every vehicle, including future ones, overriding their flat speeds. Selected.

INFRA-02.B.plain: Code keeps each vehicle's own road modifier on top of the ladder. Preserves per-vehicle character at a code cost.

INFRA-02.C.plain: Delete the flat road speeds from 14 Vanilla Vehicles Expanded vehicles. Not recommended: the per-tier setting does it better.

INFRA-02.D.plain: Write per-tier speeds on each of 14 vehicles. Keeps per-vehicle tuning, but misses any vehicle added later.

INFRA-03.Minimal.plain: Hand-authored routes instead of planned ones. Cheapest and needs no alliances, but loses 'every civilization' and extending roads farther.

INFRA-03.Middle.plain: Keeps every clause with less code than the full spec. Like it, builds nothing between factions until NPC alliances exist.

INFRA-03.As-specified.plain: A world system plans routes at each advance and lays segments over days; the half-built road is the progress bar. The most code.

INFRA-04.C1.plain: A caravan standing at a road's endpoint settlement pays in person. The earliest channel.

INFRA-04.C2.plain: The builder asks: a delivery quest with a deadline that names the road ('for the road to Ruen').

INFRA-04.C3.plain: Pledge over the comms console from Industrial, as its own radio beat. Multiplayer needs care.

INFRA-04.C4.plain: Send payment by pod or shuttle to an endpoint. The late-era channel.

INFRA-04.C5.plain: Pledge by messenger or radio, then deliver by caravan. Fits a Medieval messenger table if Medieval Overhaul ships.

INFRA-04.Gift-variant.plain: Reuse vanilla's caravan gifts. Very cheap, but funds a faction rather than a chosen road, and can't extend a road farther.

INFRA-05.H1.plain: Each faction builds at its own tech level; funding lifts a road to the era's best. Roads show each faction's tech. Recommended.

INFRA-05.H2.plain: Everyone builds one tier behind the era; only funded roads reach the top tier, so paid roads stand out everywhere.

INFRA-05.H3.plain: Buy a tier above the era, as RimPacts does. Easy in the engine, but breaks the era ceiling, so it is blocked.

INFRA-06.Build-A.plain: Use VFE Classical's road building with our tiers. Nearly free, but one research unlocks every tier unless we add a gate.

INFRA-06.Build-B.plain: Our own road-building feature. More work, but no dependency on VFE Classical.

INFRA-07.A.plain: Vehicle Framework and Vanilla Vehicles Expanded as shipped, plus fixes that stop vehicles desyncing in Multiplayer. The only alternative is no vehicles.

INFRA-07.U1.plain: Put aircraft behind their own research, so flight comes later than the first car.

INFRA-08.N1.plain: Vehicles join hostile raids and base defenders, gated on the campaign era. Revives Vehicle Framework's dormant raid feature.

INFRA-08.N2.plain: Give raiding vehicles proper armoured-assault behaviour, using Vehicle Framework's unused attack AI.

INFRA-08.N3.plain: A vehicle travels with NPC trade caravans.

INFRA-08.N4.plain: Parked, crewless vehicles at NPC sites via Worksites Expanded, a possible motor-pool prize. Multiplayer status unknown.

INFRA-08.N5.plain: Our own pre-Industrial vehicles, such as carts, with new art. The only way any vehicle exists before Industrial.

INFRA-08.N6.plain: Add vehicles to faction groups as pawns. Not recommended: with no crew they never move.

INFRA-09.A.plain: Each road tier's research unlocks a farther search band.

INFRA-09.B.plain: Vehicle research unlocks farther search bands.

INFRA-09.C.plain: A band unlocks only when a real road actually leaves the colony's tile. Truer to mobility; needs code.

ORBIT-01.A.plain: Empty orbit of everything so the view button greys out. Easy, but a ship can still fly straight up.

ORBIT-01.B.plain: A custom orbit layer that refuses viewing, flight and drawing until the reveal. True closure, but must be set before world creation.

ORBIT-01.C.plain: Block selecting orbit. Works on an existing world, but only hides it from view.

ORBIT-02.R1.plain: Remove the quest givers, or lock them behind research the reveal completes. Easy; an early uplink hack then yields nothing.

ORBIT-02.R2.plain: Givers check the reveal flag; a hacked uplink banks its coordinate and pays off at the reveal.

ORBIT-02.R3.plain: Block the givers with a patch. Works on an existing save, but an early uplink hack is wasted.

ORBIT-02.R4.plain: Point the givers at planet-side finds or lore until the reveal. Easy to close; reopening needs code.

ORBIT-02.R5.plain: World Tech Level gates them by era, not by the reveal. Backup only, and it changes a frozen setting.

ORBIT-03.Traders.plain: Orbital traders already need a comms console in vanilla; a later stage can be tied to our timing, or the event removed outright.

ORBIT-03.Salvagers.plain: Salvager raids are held back until the reveal by a check when the game picks a raiding faction.

ORBIT-04.U1.plain: Earn it however the fiction wants: a flag, a research project or a quest outcome. All write the same permanent flag.

ORBIT-05.A.plain: Orbital factions exist hidden from world creation and are unveiled together at the reveal; surface factions gain stations with history intact.

ORBIT-05.B.plain: Create factions fresh at the reveal. Not recommended: new names, leaders and ideologies, with no shared history.

ORBIT-06.A.plain: One World Tech Level definition exempting the four orbital factions and the Empire. Insurance; the faction filter itself stays off.

ORBIT-07.A.plain: The stronghold is a permanent faction settlement in orbit.

ORBIT-07.B.plain: The stronghold is a quest site, using Odyssey's abandoned-platform quest as is.

ORBIT-07.U1.plain: Hand-drawn station layouts. Not recommended: they can't hold air and are the same every visit.

ORBIT-08.S1.plain: The quest spawns the station when needed and owns it from the start. Recommended.

ORBIT-08.S2.plain: A permanent Glitterite station a quest points at. Visible beforehand, but needs the quest-site fallback if it's cleared first.

ORBIT-08.C1.plain: An objective room filled from layout data. Easy, but items can silently fail to place: fine for loot, not for plot.

ORBIT-08.C2.plain: The quest makes the exact item and places it; the quest hears when it's found, destroyed or carried off.

ORBIT-08.C4.plain: A world-side record read when the map generates. Also works for permanent settlements.

ORBIT-08.C3.plain: Vanilla's item-stash site. Not recommended: on a station it lands outside the hull or nowhere.

ORBIT-08.C5.plain: Fix the whole floor plan at quest time. Not recommended: means replacing station generation.

ORBIT-08.C6.plain: A hand-drawn station. Not recommended in orbit: it can't hold air.

ORBIT-08.E1..E4.plain: Room traps and turrets, a garrison, station guns and timed response raids, all set in data.

ORBIT-08.E5.plain: A boss mech in the objective room. Easy with Better Traders Guild; more work if ours.

ORBIT-08.RA1.plain: Trust layout rules to keep the objective room reachable. Usually works; occasionally it's sealed.

ORBIT-08.RA2.plain: After generation, check the objective exists and is reachable, and re-place it if not.

ORBIT-08.RA3.plain: Pay the prize as a reward on arrival, so nothing has to be found or carried out.

ORBIT-09.M1.plain: Leave and the site is gone; the quest resolves as its script says. Vanilla behaviour.

ORBIT-09.M2.plain: The site persists while the objective remains; returning generates a fresh map around the same item.

ORBIT-09.M3.plain: Park the gravship there and the map stays loaded indefinitely. The players' own move; nothing to build.

ORBIT-09.F1.plain: A parent quest re-offers a fresh stronghold after an interval; success retires it.

ORBIT-09.F2.plain: A failed quest immediately regenerates itself.

ORBIT-09.F3.plain: VEF's free re-grant on failure. Easy, not recommended for plot.

ORBIT-09.F4.plain: The storyteller might send another one eventually. Not recommended: no guarantee.

GRAVSHIP-01.A.plain: Odyssey and Vanilla Gravship Expanded as shipped, research retiered so habitation is Spacer, plus an alert when the deck is over budget.

GRAVSHIP-01.G.plain: Remove the standing cabin-fever mood penalty. Not recommended: the crew wanting sky is meant as a beat.

GRAVSHIP-02.A.plain: Vanilla's archite total vacuum-immunity gene. No code; how founders get it is open: archite capsule supply, or the altar's gene grant.

GRAVSHIP-03.A.plain: Our curated list of which events, conditions, factions and arrival types exist in orbit.

GRAVSHIP-03.B.plain: Vanilla Gravship Expanded's orbital hazards as shipped: solar flares, micrometeor storms, hull-punching escape pods.

GRAVSHIP-04.C.plain: Our own quests that deliver people by pod or shuttle.

GRAVSHIP-04.D.plain: Let vanilla's wanderer and refugee-pod quests fire in orbit unmodified.

GRAVSHIP-04.Build-d.plain: A small fix so two quest types still work with no surface home. Only needed if our content uses them.

GRAVSHIP-05.E.plain: Visitors and trader caravans are dropped in instead of walking across the map edge.

GRAVSHIP-05.F.plain: Shuttle to a Traders Guild station and trade there, via Better Traders Guild. Not Multiplayer-safe.

GF-A.plain: Vanilla: the ship lands on the new owner, and an ally is attacked and turns hostile. Not acceptable alone.

GF-B.plain: When our code transfers a tile, it checks the ship in flight and warns or turns it back.

GF-C.plain: Divert the ship home, to the nearest valid tile, or via crash-landing abort. A response; something else must detect.

GF-D.plain: Our transfers skip the ship's destination tile, or hold the change until it lands.

GF-E.plain: Let it happen, but warn the player while the ship is still in the air.

GF-F.plain: The changed arrival becomes the player's decision: land, move or abort, possibly leading to a parley or encounter.

GF-G.plain: At touchdown, compare the tile with what was confirmed at launch, whoever changed it, then divert, warn or ask.

GRAVSHIP-07.A.plain: Shipped shields, turrets, point defense and Ultra guns, retiered by era in data. Mortars need one small extra fix.

COLONY-01.A.plain: Checkboxes per era; unticked eras vanish from the list. Clean and short, but hides things until re-ticked. Custom code.

COLONY-01.B.plain: Current era on top, older recipes tinted, sorted below or folded into submenus. Nothing is hidden. Custom code; the spec's preferred base.

COLONY-01.C.plain: Split recipes across era-specific benches. Pure XML but re-homes ~1,420 recipes and can't keep older ones reachable. Not recommended.

COLONY-01.D.plain: Just a search box (Nice Bill Tab or our own). Easy, but has no idea of eras; only useful alongside A or B.

COLONY-01.E.plain: Patch or fork the Nice Bill Tab mod to add an era dimension. Keeps a familiar mod's UI, but hard and needs multiplayer work.

COLONY-01.F.plain: Make older recipes report themselves unavailable so they drop off the list. Changes what's on the bench, breaking the 'never a gate' rule. Not recommended.

COLONY-02.A.plain: Passion nudges the odds of each recreation choice: a drift, not a rule. Automatically covers every skill-training recreation from any mod. Spec's pick.

COLONY-02.B.plain: Hard rule: a passionate pawn always picks its passion recreation while available, falling back only when bored. More predictable, more intrusive.

COLONY-02.C.plain: Rewrite each recreation type ourselves. Same result as A with much more code to maintain. Not recommended.

COLONY-02.E.plain: Simply make all skill-training recreation more likely for everyone. Easy XML, but ignores passion entirely. Not recommended.

COLONY-02.F.plain: Rewrite vanilla's recreation picker at a low level. Reaches nothing A doesn't, at more risk. Not recommended.

COLONY-03.D.plain: Pawns reading for fun pick textbooks on their passion skills; vanilla has textbooks for all 12. Pairs with the passion drift.

COLONY-03.U1.plain: No build of its own: add new skill-training recreation (archery butt, forge game) as content and the passion preference picks it up.

DEFAULTS-01.B.plain: Apparel policies like 'Smith' ship pre-made in the Assign tab of every new colony. Always there, but carries no weapon.

DEFAULTS-01.A.plain: Kits ship as Odyssey outfit stands; the player must build and stock each stand. Physical armoury, but not ready on day one.

DEFAULTS-01.E.plain: Kits applied to spawned pawns (arrivals, quest pawns, starting colonists). Easy XML, but does nothing for pawns already in the colony.

DEFAULTS-02.A.plain: Odyssey outfit stand holds apparel plus one weapon and swaps both in one job. Easy, but one stand equips one pawn once.

DEFAULTS-02.C.plain: Use the Compositable Loadouts mod for weapons, inventory and quality rules. No multiplayer support and won't swap a held weapon. Not recommended.

DEFAULTS-02.D.plain: Our own kit system covering every clause, standing and authored. The only complete answer, and hard to build.

DEFAULTS-02.E.plain: Full kit, weapon included, on spawned pawns only. Easy XML; no help for colonists already present.

DEFAULTS-03.B.plain: Apparel policy keeps a pawn dressed over time, but assigning isn't a single act and it can't handle weapons.

DEFAULTS-03.A.plain: Outfit stand equips in one act, but only once: a pawn that later loses its weapon won't go back for it.

DEFAULTS-03.D.plain: Our own system: one act, then the pawn keeps itself kitted indefinitely. Only route meeting both halves; hard.

DEFAULTS-04.A.plain: Re-running the stand's 'Swap outfit' forces a re-gear; it only removes apparel that conflicts. Easy, but no full strip.

DEFAULTS-04.D.plain: Our own 're-equip' and 'drop everything' orders covering the whole pawn. Complete, but hard and needs multiplayer work.

DEFAULTS-05.U1.plain: Nothing to build: every kit route already tolerates future-era gear; the pawn wears its best reachable item and a stand stays partly empty.

DEFAULTS-06.A.plain: A per-recipe table of starting counts and floors applied when a bill is created. One focused code hook; skips bills that can't count products.

DEFAULTS-07.A.plain: Depend on Better Workbench Management as-is. Easy, but breaks in multiplayer and sometimes copies the material too.

DEFAULTS-07.B.plain: Use Better Workbench Management but route its paste through our multiplayer-safe command. Works in co-op; still sometimes copies material.

DEFAULTS-07.C.plain: Our own paste: we choose which settings copy, never the material, warn on skipped fields, and can paste to a whole bench. Spec's pick.

DEFAULTS-07.D.plain: Our own paste relying on Multiplayer's automatic field syncing. Same code as C but syncs less reliably. Not recommended.

DEFAULTS-07.E.plain: A shared library of named 'house standard' bill setups both players can apply. Richest option, and hard.

ITEMS-01.A.plain: Use vanilla smelting, extended to leather, cloth, wool and wood, with two reclaim recipes. Pure XML; returns the exact material.

ITEMS-02.A.plain: Declare the smelted return twice to get 50%. Pure XML; finer fractions are impossible without code.

ITEMS-03.A.plain: Already true of vanilla's return; the bill's existing durability and quality sliders do the choosing. Nothing to build.

ITEMS-04.A.plain: Reclaim bills live on the crafting spot from day one; a dedicated bench and era gate are plain XML if wanted.

ITEMS-05.A.plain: Vanilla already refuses relics and never returns advanced resources. Nothing to build.

ITEMS-06.A.plain: State the fraction in the recipe's description text. Easy; the info card can't show it correctly.

ITEMS-07.A.plain: A small custom counter, modelled on vanilla's stone-block one, so the bill can target a stock level. About 30 lines of code.

SPECIALISATION-01.A.plain: At skill thresholds, pick one entry from a list for that skill. The lightest of the full systems; spec's base.

SPECIALISATION-01.B.plain: A branching tree with tiers; taking one branch closes its sibling (weapons vs armour). Stronger identity, more to build.

SPECIALISATION-01.C.plain: A perk catalogue whose perks can do more than tweak a stat, e.g. extra yield on one recipe. Most flexible effects; hard.

SPECIALISATION-01.D.plain: One board showing every option and unspent points, with an alert when points await. Makes the pick feel like a moment.

SPECIALISATION-02.A..D.plain: Our own specialisation system simply checks for a major passion before allowing the pick.

SPECIALISATION-02.E.plain: Specialist posts get a custom role requirement demanding major passion in the skill.

SPECIALISATION-02.F.plain: The 'trained' health condition gets a small check that refuses pawns without the major passion.

SPECIALISATION-02.G.plain: A trait links to passion in XML, but backwards: generation gives the pawn the passion to fit the trait.

SPECIALISATION-03.U1.plain: Every route already works as small stat bonuses; only the perk-catalogue route can reach effects a stat can't express.

SPECIALISATION-04.XML.plain: Add new weapon- and armour-smithing speed stats and point the recipes at them. Pure data, identical on both clients.

SPECIALISATION-04.Csharp.plain: Code that knows which recipe is being made and applies the bonus accordingly (the perk catalogue's approach).

SPECIALISATION-05.A..D.plain: At pawn generation, roll specialisations from the pawn's final skills and passions, skipping starting colonists. Keyed on actual skill.

SPECIALISATION-05.F.plain: Give pawn types a starting 'trained' condition in XML. Easy, but tied to the pawn type, not its actual skills.

SPECIALISATION-05.G.plain: Force a trait via backstory or pawn type. XML, but the pawn's skills get shaped to fit the trait rather than vice versa.

SPECIALISATION-05.E.plain: Not possible: generated pawns never hold Ideology roles.

SPECIALISATION-06.E.plain: Vanilla Ideology specialist roles. Easy in XML but capped at two post types with unlimited holders; one-holder seats and passion gates need code.

SPECIALISATION-07.E.plain: One role per pawn; switching posts means running the role-change ritual. Pure XML.

SPECIALISATION-07.F.plain: A 'trained as weaponsmith' health entry, granted by surgery, item or rite and removed by surgery; visible in the Health tab. Easy.

SPECIALISATION-07.G.plain: Make it a trait, reading as who the pawn is rather than training. More work than F. Not recommended over F.

QUESTS-01.A.plain: A permanent, auto-accepted parent quest that generates each Chronicle beat as a child. Built on vanilla's sub-quest system, no engine patching.

QUESTS-02.P.plain: Each subplot's parent quest is fired as a standing quest by a named event. Easy XML.

QUESTS-02.N1.plain: Attach steps to their parent only where we grant them ourselves (Schism catalogue, shop purchases). Misses other channels.

QUESTS-02.N2.plain: One hook tags any quest to its parent whatever delivered it: storyteller, giver, chains. Covers every channel; spec's pick with P.

QUESTS-02.N3.plain: VEF's quest-chain badge icon. Easy but only an icon, not real nesting.

QUESTS-03.A.plain: Only a successful beat advances the story; an expired or lost one leaves the same beat next in line. Already specced.

QUESTS-04.A.plain: Vanilla already shows a 3 / 9 count on the parent and indents live beats beneath it. Free.

QUESTS-04.T1.plain: As shipped: the parent's detail pane lists finished beats. Easy, but finished beats leave the list itself.

QUESTS-04.T2.plain: Write a live beat list into the parent quest's description text. Modest code, no UI patching.

QUESTS-04.T3.plain: Patch the quest tab to draw finished and upcoming beats under their parent. Most legible; touches vanilla UI.

QUESTS-05.C1.plain: Add a difficulty rating to each quest definition, patchable onto any mod's quest. Easy but must be done quest by quest.

QUESTS-05.C2.plain: Automatically give any unrated quest a fallback rating from its threat points. Catches everything; needs code.

QUESTS-05.C3.plain: A load-time check that lists unrated quests so they can be fixed. Easy; a tool, not a fix.

QUESTS-06.A.plain: Vanilla's quest letter accepts free text for its body; supply the reason, or name the asking leader.

QUESTS-07.U1.plain: One XML line puts any quest into Charting's survey pool and keeps it out of the random storyteller. Easy.

QUESTS-07.A.plain: One era check flips a quest from charted to self-announcing when the colony reaches a named era. Code; multiplayer-safe.

QUESTS-07.B.plain: Two copies of each quest plus a World Tech Level setting, for quests a named event delivers. Easy XML, but relies on a mod setting.

QUESTS-08.A.plain: Main story runs as a fixed ordered list; each discovery pool has a guaranteed-find timer that Charting work matures.

QUESTS-09.Storyteller-pool.plain: Quest joins the storyteller's random pool from a set earliest day, drawn by weight. Easy XML; timing is loose.

QUESTS-09.World-object.plain: Found via the Charting apparatus, or rolled by caravans and outposts as they travel.

QUESTS-09.Named-incident.plain: Fire a specific quest on a fixed day (easy XML), or our own trigger once a condition holds (code).

QUESTS-10.G1.plain: The quest's giver is a random non-hostile faction. Easy XML.

QUESTS-10.G2.plain: A named faction leader asks, with certain factions excluded. Easy XML; more personal.

QUESTS-10.G3.plain: Choose givers by a goodwill threshold or by tech level/culture. Finer control; needs our code.

QUESTS-10.GT.plain: Tag a quest so traders, books or orbital scans hand it over. One XML line; needs Odyssey, and bypasses the usual can-it-run checks.

QUESTS-11.A.plain: Each Church decree defines its own failure penalty: mood, Exaltation or goodwill. Easy with Deserters, moderate without.

QUESTS-11.B.plain: One patch stops decrees arriving while the Church is hostile. Easy XML.

QUESTS-11.C.plain: A generic failure-cost hook in code. Nothing for it to reach. Not recommended.

QUESTS-11.D.plain: Church decrees arrive on a schedule instead of only from a noble's mental break. XML for conceited titleholders only, else code.

QUESTS-12.Build-A.plain: Build on VEF's quest-giver shop with our currencies and window. About 95 lines; spec's pick.

QUESTS-12.Build-B.plain: Our own shop from scratch, about 260 lines. Harder; the fallback if the VEF dependency is refused.

QUESTS-13.A.plain: One shelf; items sold as quests that reward the item, with XML eligibility and per-entry expiry. Easy.

QUESTS-13.B.plain: Entries leave individually when expired or ineligible and restock one at a time, rather than the whole shelf refreshing.

QUESTS-13.C.plain: A condition check reading era, a currency balance or a political flag. Needs re-checking at purchase to be multiplayer-safe.

QUESTS-13.D.plain: Separate shelves for missions and items. Cleaner layout, more to build.

QUESTS-13.E.plain: Reskin a vanilla trader as the shop. Hard, and traders can't sell quests. Not recommended.

QUESTS-14.A.plain: A fresh copy of the failed mission restocks the same shelf, free or priced, set per entry. Spec's pick.

QUESTS-14.B.plain: Refund all or part of the price on failure, as a per-entry option of the same piece.

QUESTS-14.C.plain: VEF sends a free copy later as an ordinary offer. Easy XML, but unsuited to plot missions.

QUESTS-14.D.plain: The Schism simply re-offers its current plot step. Already specified.

QUESTS-14.E.plain: Adopt VFE Deserters' shop wholesale. Hard, and its failed missions never return. Not recommended.

QUESTS-15.U1.plain: No build: Multiplayer already syncs accepting quests and picking rewards.
